changes.after: A lifetime describes how long a borrow may be used.

before: A lifetime parameter such as 'a relates borrowed inputs to a borrowed output. It does not extend any object’s life or choose how long memory physically exists.

Both arguments and the returned slice use 'a below because either input may be returned. The caller must keep whichever reference the contract permits valid for the result’s use. Annotations describe the guarantee; they do not make a local String live forever.
Expected output or behavior: first. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

after: A lifetime describes how long a borrow may be used.
The same mark on the two inputs and the result means the returned view must work whichever input is picked. It does not keep either String alive longer.
